text.text: Real Madrid pulled off a historic and unprecedented comeback in the Champions League, turning a 3-1 deficit against Roma into a thrilling 4-3 win after an extraordinary revival in the closing minutes. Three goals in quick succession did it. Carlos Espi struck on 82:04, Endrick followed on 84:40 and Antonio Rudiger completed the job on 89:47, flipping a two-goal deficit into a one-goal lead. A statistic published by MisterChip put the whole turnaround at 7 minutes and 43 seconds, the fastest away comeback in Champions League history. The Spanish giants broke a record that belonged to Liverpool, who took 12 minutes and 48 seconds to overturn their deficit against Villarreal when the two teams met on 3 May 2022. text.text: Bellingham achieved his 100th victory with the Real Madrid jersey against Roma, and he did so in his 150th match as a madridista. The midfielder reaches both milestones in his fourth season with our club, during which he has scored 49 goals. Since his debut on August 12, 2023, he has won five titles: 1 Champions League, 1 Club World Cup, 1 UEFA Super Cup, 1 La Liga, and 1 Spanish Super Cup. His 150 matches are distributed as follows: 95 in La Liga, 35 in the Champions League, 6 in the Copa del Rey, 7 in the Club World Cup, 6 in the Spanish Super Cup, and 1 in the UEFA Super Cup. Regarding victories, he has accumulated 67 in La Liga, 20 in the Champions League, 3 in the Copa del Rey, 5 in the Club World Cup, 4 in the Spanish Super Cup, and 1 in the UEFA Super Cup. His best season in terms of records was 2024/25 (58 matches and 37 wins). The opponent he has faced the most is Atlético de Madrid (11), while the teams he has defeated the most times are Alavés and Villarreal (6). text.text: New Zealand’s white-ball captain Mitchell Santner is banking on home conditions to help his team counter India’s formidable batting line-up as the sides prepare for a demanding multi-format series, beginning with five T20Is on October 22.Earlier this year, India beat New Zealand 4-1 in their bilateral T20I series at home before defeating them in the T20 World Cup final, also on home soil. But Santner believes the change in conditions will give the Kiwis an opportunity to turn the tables.“We know how good India are,” Santner said during an interaction arranged by Sony Sports Network. “They’re so good at playing in their home conditions and on those grounds, and it’s the same for us. We know how to operate in New Zealand, so I think that gives us a little bit of an edge.”Santner, however, is wary of the damage India can inflict if the surfaces are flat and the boundaries short, conditions that have increasingly favoured aggressive batting in white-ball cricket. The French engineer was promoted from Racing Bulls in July 2025 and led the Milton Keynes-based outfit through a challenging start to this year, which saw them drop behind their rivals under the new regulations. However, their consistent work over the course of 2026 – guided by Mekies – finally paid off as Max Verstappen secured back-to-back victories in Malaysia and Singapore, bringing Red Bull back into contention for regular wins. I wasn't thinking about making the same serve as Djokovic. But at the end, I can even see the similarities. "I think everyone has to make changes, small details. For me, the serve is something that I really want to be better every year, in every tournament. I'm just putting constant work on the serve." why: Internazionale beaten by Club Brugge at home

report.text: Club Brugge and their young forward Nicolò Tresoldi shocked Inter 4-3 at San Siro in the Champions League’s result of the night. Tresoldi, a 22-year-old Italian-born Germany Under-21s forward, scored the first three goals for the Belgian side. A Hakan Calhanoglu foul on Carlos Forbs resulted in a penalty which Tresoldi slotted in just before the half hour. Tresoldi picked up his second after capitalising on a blunder by the Inter keeper Josep Martínez and reacted faster than the Inter defence for the third with a quarter of an hour to go. Lautaro Martínez had given his team a lifeline just before the break after a move initiated by Marcus Thuram, followed by a Federico Dimarco back-heel assist. report.text: RIYADH: Cristiano Ronaldo scored Al-Nassr's second goal as the Saudi Pro League champions overcame an hour-long security delay to beat Uzbekistan's Neftchi 3-1 in the Asian Champions League Elite on Monday. Kick-off was delayed after Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence issued a safety warning 15 minutes before the scheduled start time in Riyadh, which has been targeted by missiles fired from Yemen-based Houthis in recent days. Ange Postecoglou's side shook off the interruption and went ahead through Angelo in the 33rd minute with a deflected strike, before Ronaldo doubled the lead nine minutes later. The 41-year-old struck after Sadio Mane delivered a looping cross from the left that Aiman Yahya directed into Ronaldo's path with his chest, and the Portuguese forward lashed the ball into the bottom corner with a shot on the turn. Alisher Odilov pulled one back for Neftchi six minutes into the second half, but Ikromjon Alibaev's red card for a foul on Mohamed Simakan in the 65th minute, and an own goal by Anvarjon Gofurov 13 minutes later sealed the win for Al-Nassr. report.text: HYDERABAD, India (AP) — Shai Hope set a West Indies record by reaching 102 not out as West Indies beat India by 24 runs Wednesday in the fourth cricket T20 to level the five-match series at 2-2.Hope hit nine sixes and four fours in his third T20 century – the most for a West Indies batter – as the visitors piled up 247-3 in 20 overs. India had won the toss and opted to bowl.It was the second-highest first innings total in T20s against India, trailing England’s 257-3 in Southampton this year.In reply, Sanju Samson hit 56 off 23 balls but India was down to 130-5 and the chase never took off. It finished with 223 in 19.3 overs.Keemo Paul picked 5-41 for his second five-wicket haul in T20s.Bengaluru will host the deciding T20 on Saturday.Put into bat, Hope gave West Indies a flying by putting on 52 off 26 balls with Jewel Andrew (21). Axar Patel trapped Andrew lbw in the fifth over but West Indies still got 79-1 in the powerplay.Hope then added another 58 off 24 balls with Shimron Hetmyer, reaching 50 off 28 balls with the help of five sixes. report.text: Carlos Alcaraz reflected on his Shanghai Masters defeat after losing to Zizou Bergs 7-5, 7-6(4) in the round of 32 and admitted he struggled to find his best level. Carlos Alcaraz suffered a surprising defeat against Belgium’s Zizou Bergs in the round of 32 at the Shanghai Masters. Bergs won 7-5, 7-6(4) to claim one of the biggest victories of his career. Alcaraz was unhappy with his performance and admitted that he made too many mistakes. The Spaniard also gave credit to Bergs for playing well and serving strongly. Alcaraz could not find his rhythm against Bergs. The Belgian took his chances and stayed calm during the important points. He won the first set 7-5 but then bergs held his nerve in the second-set tie-break to win the match. The Spaniard felt that his own performance was below his usual level. He also said that Bergs benefited from a few lucky shots but made good use of those moments. “Today it wasn’t a good match for my side. I didn’t play good. report.text: Golden State turned a tight night into a runaway, beating the Los Angeles Lakers 152-114 at Crypto.com Arena in the NBA Preseason . The crowd of 7,471 got a little bit of everything, from hot shooting bursts to a turnover storm late. The Warriors pulled away with a ferocious fourth quarter built on pressure defense and second chances. For full box score details and play-by-play, see the game page on Sofascore . The first quarter offered balance, finishing level at 29-29. By halftime, Golden State had nudged in front 101-88 after a high-paced second period. The Warriors then kept the momentum through the third, taking a 123-101 lead into the final frame. Los Angeles needed a spark, but Golden State instead found another gear. The fourth quarter was all Warriors, 29-13, and the gap ballooned as the minutes ticked down. In short, the night started even, tilted by halftime, and then tipped decisively late. The Warriors’ closing kick separated the teams. Los Angeles could not match the pace or the possession battle over the final 12 minutes. report.text: On a night dominated by the apparent status of Kristaps Porzingis, the absence of the Latvian big was felt at times during the Golden State Warriors’ 101-89 win over the Los Angeles Lakers at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada. Steve Kerr’s intention to spread the floor in a so-called ‘5-out’ alignment banked on players who are able to space to floor — including their center. Porzingis happens to fit that profile, while also being 7-foot-3-inches. Without Porzingis — and also not having Al Horford available tonight — the Warriors were not only small, they were bereft of shooting and spacing personnel. That was apparent at times during this game, where the Warriors were able to rally back from a significant deficit, albeit during a time when both teams’ main characters’ nights were finished (one of them, Luka Doncic, did not suit up for the Lakers). Once again, it was rookie Yaxel Lendeborg who stood out. He finished with 17 points, 5 rebounds, and 4 assists in just under 24 minutes of time on the floor.
